scope: Phoenix-2014T train-only selection followed by one frozen retrospective dev confirmation; test forbidden
question: Which temporal input construction gives the best implementable WER/latency tradeoff for the current ISLR plus online CSLR pipeline?

selection_protocol.confirmation_split: dev, exactly once after candidate and decoder are frozen
guardrails: insertion component must not erase the DEL+SUB gain

stages.name: implementation and coordinate audit
stages.promotion: all input/foreground coordinates are understood and any mismatch is quantified

stages.name: frozen-checkpoint input sensitivity
stages.promotion: candidate improves short-gloss top-1 or correct-class margin without a broad common-gloss regression

stages.name: equal-budget short fine-tuning
stages.budget: same initialization, optimizer steps, gloss bags and random seeds
stages.promotion: stable source-disjoint train gain on isolated diagnostics and continuous WER

stages.name: full training for promoted candidates
stages.budget: same 100-epoch ceiling and stopping rule as baseline
stages.promotion: Pareto improvement in WER, short-gloss errors, latency and complexity

stages.name: single frozen dev confirmation
stages.promotion: source-cluster interval and error decomposition support the preregistered direction

candidate_interpretation.B_only_wins: padding or foreground aggregation is the leading mechanism
candidate_interpretation.C_wins: adjacent motion or context-label mixing is the leading mechanism
candidate_interpretation.D_wins: proxy boundaries omit useful sign evidence
candidate_interpretation.E_wins: one fixed temporal scale is mismatched
candidate_interpretation.none_win: audit boundary quality, intrinsic short-sign ambiguity and domain shift before variable-length engineering

variable_length_gate: Implement true variable-length batching only if bucketed/masked evidence beats every fixed-16 construction and the gain exceeds its measured latency/complexity cost.
